title: Installing Arduino Core and ESP-IDF

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “Installing Arduino Core and ESP-IDF” to a real program or device. The key principle is: ESP-IDF selects the chip target before building. In a project, follow this guidance: Keep board package, toolchain, and framework versions stable while diagnosing a first build.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
EXAMPLE CODE

spans.code:
idf.py --version
idf.py set-target esp32
idf.py build

spans.text: EXPECTED RESULT
Flash and monitor output depends on a connected board, selected serial port, target, and firmware.
CORE EXPLANATION
Arduino-ESP32 offers the familiar sketch model. ESP-IDF is Espressif's component-based CMake/Kconfig and FreeRTOS framework; choose for project needs and pin the version.
idf.py
commands are specific to an ESP-IDF project and toolchain. Arduino-ESP32 uses its own Arduino CLI/IDE board package and build workflow; these commands are not Arduino sketch commands.
IMPORTANT LINE BREAKDOWN
Key line:
idf.py --version

What it does: ESP-IDF selects the chip target before building.
Why it is used: Keep board package, toolchain, and framework versions stable while diagnosing a first build.
If omitted or changed: ESP-IDF Installation Manager and official setup guides provide OS-specific toolchain steps.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Skipping this check before applying the rule: Keep board package, toolchain, and framework versions stable while diagnosing a first build.
REMEMBER
ESP-IDF selects the chip target before building.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Keep board package, toolchain, and framework versions stable while diagnosing a first build.
Equivalent Arduino CLI setup

spans.code:
arduino-cli core update-index
arduino-cli core install esp32:esp32
